status: Verified isolated relational foundation; not a complete business migration

pending.existing_full_design: preparation/schema-design.json remains the conceptual model for all entities; unimplemented tables in that file are proposals, not created tables.
pending.ordering: Complete catalog and dataset-scope contracts before dependent financial tables. Then implement coherent command groups with receipts and audit: product+versions+links; sale+customer+receipt; subscription+price snapshot+sale+event+receipt; expense+allocations+payment; transfer+both account amounts; import event+dedup record+all effects.
invariants: A receipt cannot be recreated by restoring a sale
A retry cannot duplicate any side effect
Historical subscription prices do not change when current plans change
Never total unmatched currencies as if converted
Expense allocation preserves the global total
Transfers preserve both currencies and explicit amounts
A failed integration event leaves no customer, sale or subscription partial changes
pending.financial_policy_pending: Characterize original refund/void/paid-expense behavior before implementing SQL finance; do not silently change historical totals or turn commercial refunds into inferred cash movements.

future_restore_wipe.activation_gate: Not available in the SQL API until all business modules, complete JSON validation and end-to-end tests are implemented. Existing browser buttons are unchanged.
future_restore_wipe.scope: A future SQL restore/wipe applies to one complete business environment shared by all sessions, never a partial browser-local subset. Authentication, credentials and other environments are excluded.
future_restore_wipe.backup: Consistent complete SQL snapshot plus manifest with schema version, environment/dataset revision, counts and checksums; exclude passwords, sessions and local PIN. This is distinct from the private synthetic pre-migration SQL dump used by this block.
future_restore_wipe.preview: Validate all collections, types, enum values, IDs, duplicate normalized keys, relationships, money, dates and unsupported fields before writes. Report differences, conflicts, missing exchange rates and historical unknowns; do not invent history or silently discard fields.
future_restore_wipe.restore: Require preview bound to backup checksum and expected dataset revision, explicit confirmation and stable operation ID. Save a private destination backup first. Stage a complete replacement dataset, verify counts/amounts/balances/references, then atomically switch the active dataset pointer. Retain the prior dataset read-only for recovery; never replay createSale to reconstruct old receipts.
future_restore_wipe.wipe: Require explicit environment confirmation and expected dataset revision, private prior backup and stable operation ID. Atomically switch to a new empty dataset for that environment, retaining the old dataset read-only. Other environments and authentication remain unchanged.
future_restore_wipe.prerequisite_migration: Dataset generations and active-dataset pointers, including generation scope in entity FKs and command receipts, must be added and tested before restore/wipe or financial activation. This first-block schema has only environment scope and cannot yet implement these operations safely.
future_restore_wipe.browser: No automatic deletion or import. Legacy backups require explicit staged migration; server preview conflicts must be resolved before activation. Existing browser data remains available until a separately reviewed complete cutover.

risks: MariaDB tested; Oracle MySQL/Hostinger not tested
Nontransactional DDL needs private backup and manual partial-schema recovery
No legacy JSON import, financial services or SQL restore/wipe yet; equivalence not claimed for unimplemented modules
